description: Universal Digital Twin: Land use is a software platform described in the paper "Universal Digital Twin: Land use" in Data-Centric Engineering (Cambridge University Press, 2022), produced by Jethro Akroyd, Zachary Harper, David Soutar and colleagues. This article develops an ontological description of land use and applies it to incorporate geospatial information describing land coverage into a knowledge-graph-based Universal Digital Twin. Sources of data relating to land use in the UK have been surveyed. The Crop Map of England (CROME) is produced annually by the UK Government and was identified as a valuable source of open data. Coverage: England, from the Crop Map of England. Access is through the paper, which is available online; the paper describes the tool and its use cases, and no separate code link was verified, so the paper is the only link. Licence: not stated (data set page not reachable on 2026-10-01; the paper is CC-BY-4.0). Cost: no charge is stated in the metadata read; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support cross-domain digital twin studies that combine land use with energy scenarios. Related: the paper is the Data-Centric Engineering article 10.1017/dce.2021.21.
